title: K6-PerfFramework Runtime Settings
description: Controls think time, pacing, HTTP behavior, error handling, reporting, error capture, host monitoring, and debug mode for all test executions. Most fields are optional — sensible defaults are applied by the framework (see FRAMEWORK_DEFAULTS in ConfigContracts.ts).

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editor IntelliSense (ignored at runtime).

thinkTime.description: Simulates user think time (pause) between transaction groups. Applied automatically in generated/converted scripts via sleep(getFrameworkThinkTime()). Realistic think times improve load accuracy by mimicking real user behavior.

ignoreThinkTime.description: If true, skips think time (sleep) entirely regardless of other settings.

globalOverride.description: If true, forces the global think time settings (fixed or random) to override any specific think time values provided in the script.

mode.description:
fixed — constant delay of 'fixed' seconds between every transaction group.
random — uniform random delay between 'min' and 'max' seconds.
Tip: Use 'random' for realistic production simulations; 'fixed' for deterministic debugging.

fixed.description: Think time in seconds when mode='fixed'. Ignored when mode='random'. Example: 1 = one-second pause between transactions.

min.description: Minimum think time in seconds when mode='random'. Must be less than 'max'. Example: 0.5 = half-second minimum pause.

max.description: Maximum think time in seconds when mode='random'. Must be greater than 'min'. Example: 3 = up to three seconds pause.

pacing.description: Iteration-level rate control. When enabled, the framework ensures each iteration takes at least 'targetIntervalSeconds' — adding sleep at the end if the iteration finishes early. This prevents VU 'bunching' under light load. Similar to LoadRunner Pacing.

enabled.description: Enable iteration pacing. When false, VUs start the next iteration immediately after the previous one completes.

targetIntervalSeconds.description: Target duration in seconds for one complete iteration (init → action → end). If the iteration finishes faster, the remaining time is added as a sleep. Example: 30 = each iteration takes at least 30 seconds.

http.description: Global HTTP request defaults applied to all k6 HTTP calls. These can be overridden per-request in individual scripts.

timeoutSeconds.description: Global HTTP request timeout in seconds. Requests exceeding this duration are aborted. Tip: Set higher (120+) for API endpoints with heavy processing; lower (10–30) for fast UI pages.

maxRedirects.description: Maximum number of HTTP redirects to follow automatically. Set to 0 to disable redirect following (useful for testing redirect logic explicitly).

throwOnError.description: When true, non-2xx HTTP responses throw an exception that triggers the errorBehavior handler. When false, non-2xx responses are silently returned (check status in your script). Tip: Set true for strict testing; false when you need to assert specific error codes.

errorBehavior.description:
What happens when an error occurs during script execution.
• continue — Log the error and keep running (best for load tests where some errors are expected).
• stop_iteration — Skip remaining actions in this iteration, start the next one (good for data-dependent flows).
• stop_vu — Terminate this virtual user permanently (strict mode).
• abort_test — Halt the entire test immediately (use for critical-path validation).

reporting.description: Controls what appears in the generated RunReport.html and console transaction table. These settings do NOT affect k6's native summary output.

transactionStats.description: Which statistical columns to show in the transaction metrics table. Common values: count, pass, fail, avg, min, max, p(50), p(75), p(90), p(95), p(97), p(99). Example: ["count", "pass", "fail", "avg", "p(90)", "p(95)"].

includeTransactionTable.description: Include the transaction metrics matrix in the generated HTML report and console output.

includeErrorTable.description: Include the error summary table in the generated HTML report.

overrideExistingResults.description: When true, debug and load-test reports overwrite a single stable 'Run_latest' output folder each run instead of creating a new timestamped folder. Off by default so run history is preserved.

timeseries.description: Bucketed timeseries data collection for interactive Chart.js graphs in RunReport.html. Produces time-bucketed response time trends, throughput, and error rate charts.

enabled.description: Enable timeseries data collection. When disabled, the report will not include time-based trend charts.

bucketSizeSeconds.description: Aggregation bucket size in seconds for timeseries data points. Smaller = more granular charts but larger data. Default 1 produces per-second resolution on every overview/transaction/system chart; raise to 5–10 for >30-min runs or 30–60 for hour-plus soaks if HTML size becomes an issue.

keepRawMetricsStream.description: Retain the raw k6 streaming-JSON output file (`metrics-stream.json`) in the run folder after the unified report finishes. When `false`, the file is deleted automatically — useful for CI / storage-constrained environments. When `true` (default), it stays for ad-hoc re-analysis. The file can be tens to hundreds of MB for long high-RPS runs.

errors.description: Error capture and request/response snapshot settings. When a check() assertion fails, the framework can capture a full snapshot of the HTTP exchange for post-run debugging.

captureSnapshotOnFailure.description: When true, failed check() assertions trigger a full request/response snapshot capture. Snapshots are included in the RunReport.html for post-run debugging.

maxSnapshotsPerRun.description: Maximum number of snapshots to capture per test run. Prevents excessive memory/disk usage during high-error-rate tests. Set to 0 to disable snapshot capture entirely.

includeRequestHeaders.description: Include HTTP request headers in captured snapshots.

includeRequestBody.description: Include HTTP request body in captured snapshots. Disable for privacy-sensitive payloads.

includeResponseHeaders.description: Include HTTP response headers in captured snapshots.

includeResponseBody.description: Include HTTP response body in captured snapshots. Warning: Can produce large snapshots for HTML/JSON-heavy responses. Enable selectively.

monitoring.description: Runner-side host monitoring. Captures CPU and memory usage of the machine running k6 during the test. Produces warnings if resource usage exceeds thresholds — helps detect when the load generator itself is the bottleneck.

enabled.description: Enable host resource monitoring during test execution. Adds system metrics to RunReport.html.

cpuWarningPercent.description: CPU usage warning threshold (%). If the load generator exceeds this, a warning is generated. Rule of thumb: Keep below 80% to avoid k6 itself becoming the bottleneck.

memoryWarningPercent.description: Memory usage warning threshold (%). High memory usage may indicate VU data leaks or excessive snapshot capture.

sampleIntervalSeconds.description: How often to sample CPU/memory metrics in seconds. Lower = more data points but slightly more overhead.

debugMode.description: Enable debug mode. When true: prints the fully resolved configuration at startup, enables verbose lifecycle logging, and adds extra diagnostic output. Useful for troubleshooting config resolution issues. Should be false in CI/CD pipelines.
